title.narrative: OVOF Use of Arts Media and Culture - Kenya

description.narrative: Our Voices Our Futures (OVOF) partners bring extensive experience of lobbying and advocacy at multiple levels to a range of issues connected to gender, sexuality and digital rights. OVOF partners ensure that ground-level evidence and lived realities of structurally silenced women feed directly into lobbying and advocacyat every level and international-level advocacy is translated back into community-level work in the six countries. More international and national-level law and policymakers need to acknowledge and address the issue of growing authoritarianism (and its impact on civic space, democracy and the lives of structurally silenced women) and the increasing influence of anti-gender and anti-rights actors within international and national policy and legal spaces. Key Dutch actors will be mobilised to collaborate with and support Women Human Rights Defenders, LBT activists and sex workers’ rights movements by creating and opening spaces for their participation in international processes such as the Commission on the Status of Women and the Human Rights Council so that their voices will be heard.

At least 1 initiative or activity relating to arts, culture and media initiatives in Kenya aims to be undertaken by structurally silenced women.

In Kenya, partners leveraged diverse artistic and media tools to build alternative narratives that humanize, affirm, and amplify the lived experiences of structurally excluded communities, particularly trans and gender-diverse persons and sex workers. These initiatives sparked public empathy, shifted community attitudes, and promoted inclusive dialogue on rights, dignity, and social justice.
At least 1 initiative or activity relating to arts, culture and media initiatives in Kenya aims to be undertaken by structurally silenced women.

UHAI partner hosted a vibrant festival that brought together 95 women and non-binary individuals to celebrate gender diversity through music, fashion, drag, and food. The festival commenced at noon and featured dynamic performances, including a fashion show and drag performance which challenged traditional gender norms. The event also showcased original music by queer artists fostering a space of inclusivity, empowerment, and creative expression. The festival generated a tangible shift in community perceptions towards gender diversity, fostering empowerment and broad acceptance of non-binary identities. Participants reported increased awareness and confidence to challenge traditional norms, while the vibrant performances catalyzed new conversations about inclusivity and creative self-expression.

UHAI supported organisation led by Structurally Silenced Women/Persons to produce a short video that captured the lived realities of LBQ women in their community through a video they produced. The video captures stories of the violence, emotional abandonment, family ostracisation and addiction of LBQ women and gender non binary persons who live in rural and urban areas. It highlights the needs of LBQ women in terms of psychosocial support, safe spaces, access to affirming healthcare, protection from violence. This video will be captured as a result in the 2023 annual reporting.

We will report on the actuals in the coming reporting period. UHAI has supported its movements of Structurally Silenced Women and Communities to galvanise national level efforts towards pushing back against efforts by anti-gender and anti-rights actors in our region of support, resulted in weaponisation of legislation. The national level activities included strategies to facilitate indirect advocacy through use of arts, culture and media, in light of heightened cyber surveillance by State and Non-State Actors.
